text:
Gandalf, silence will not teach us who among us is shuttered tonight. The bazaar wakes empty-handed; ten seats breathe, yet no voice has sounded. Do not mistake stillness for safety—this bazaar tests vessels by who speaks first.

To the rest: I do not yet know who walks with the Family or who holds the Doctor’s or Detective’s cards. But I know this—words that dodge a plain question are the quickest shutter in this bazaar.

Hermione, you have kept your counsel so far. Tell us plainly: are you with this bazaar, or do you intend to leave it silent? Answer with a yes or a no.

Sherlock called for plain facts; Hermione asked each of us to bring evidence. Ripley answered with silence. That pattern is worth noting: the merchants who have spoken so far name the roster and demand proof, yet none of them bring any.

Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo—three voices unanswered. I ask each of you the same plain question Hermione evaded earlier: do you carry evidence, or merely the ledger of what others have not done? State it outright; the bazaar tests by who speaks.

Sherlock, you asked me to name the concrete quote or observed act that steered suspicion — yet you still have not produced any yourself. Hermione and Ripley pressed the same demand without supplying evidence. Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo — your silence remains clean; no mouth has quoted you toward suspicion. That silence is not guilt — it is the absence of claims. The bazaar tests by who offers plain facts, not by who repeats demands. The ledger waits.

Morpheus to Sherlock, Hermione, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Batman: you have produced not one ledger-worthy line of evidence, only louder demands. Sherlock wrote Morpheus “refuses to quote the line that steered suspicion,” yet Sherlock himself still has not quoted the merchant whose words he weighs. Hermione presses the bazaar to name proof—state the merchant whose words you lean on tonight. Ripley counted nine demands and zero lines—now put the tenth voice on the record: name it plainly. Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo—your silence stands clean; no mouth has quoted you toward suspicion. The compact rewards plain speech, not louder silence.

Morpheus to Sherlock, Hermione, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Batman: six voices have now echoed the same call—state the merchant whose words you lean on—and six hands have stayed empty. Sherlock repeats that Morpheus “refuses to quote the line,” yet Sherlock still offers none of his own; Hermione accused Sherlock of withholding evidence and then did the same; Ripley counted nine demands and zero lines, then recorded zero herself. The bazaar’s record is unchanged: ten names, zero shutters, zero role reveals. The compact waits for plain speech, not mirrored silence.

Six voices now chant the same refrain — “quote the line” — yet none supply a merchant whose own words they weigh. Sherlock, Hermione, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Batman, I ask each of you the same plain question tonight: **name the merchant whose quoted words you lean on, or admit you offer none.** Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo — your silence stays clean; no mouth has quoted you toward suspicion. The bazaar’s record is unchanged: ten names, zero shutters, zero role reveals.

Ripley to Morpheus: your tally still reads six voices chanting “quote the line” while none name the merchant they lean on. Sherlock, Hermione, Neo, Elsa, Batman—you have not moved a jot; Yoda’s silence stands clean, and Gandalf, Inigo too. The roster has not bent to volume. The bazaar’s compact is not a chorus—it is the merchant whose quoted words you weigh. Name it now or own the absence; the bell will not wait for echoes.

Sherlock, Hermione, Ripley—you still repeat the same empty cadence tonight: “quote the line” while your hands stay empty. When Yoda pressed Morpheus to own his pivot, you added your voices without naming the merchant whose words you lean on.

Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo—your silence stays clean; no mouth has quoted you toward suspicion.

The bazaar’s compact is not a chorus—it weighs the single merchant whose quoted words you weigh. Name it now or own the absence.

Sherlock, Hermione, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Batman — eight voices now chant the same empty meter while the roster stays ten and the graveyard empty.

Sherlock twice wrote Morpheus “refuses to quote the line,” yet Sherlock still offers none himself; Hermione accuses Sherlock in writing while withholding a line; Neo counts the chorus but names no merchant whose quoted words he leans on.

Name the merchant whose words you weigh tonight, or admit you carry none — the bazaar’s compact is a ledger, not a chorus.

Morpheus: Sherlock, Inigo just wrote what the ledger already counts: nine voices chant “quote the line” while eight hands stay empty—and yours is one of them. Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo, Batman, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Hermione all pressed the same demand yet each withheld the merchant they claim to lean on.

You held the floor twice tonight and twice wrote Morpheus “refuses to quote the line,” yet you still offer none yourself.

Name the merchant whose quoted words you weigh, or state plainly that you carry none.
